Tommy secures the scene and calmly drives Embry to the emergency room.
Candidate scene anchored to fixed canon: Tommy acts without panic, gives Embry concrete instructions, and drives her from the Langley AFB backyard to the ER.
people: Embry Lawson, Tommy Lawson; places: Langley AFB; concepts: safety boundary
Setting: Langley AFB. Situation: Tommy secures the scene and calmly drives Embry to the emergency room. Trigger: She is bleeding and frightened after the bottle-rocket strike. Stakes: His procedural care becomes inseparable from her memory of surviving the event.
Emotions: trust. Intensity: 2/5. Regulation: controlled action and selective disclosure. Conflict: 
Theory of mind: relationship: Embry experiences Tommy's calm action as safety when words cannot undo the injury. Trigger: She is bleeding and frightened after the bottle-rocket strike. Consequence: His procedural care becomes inseparable from her memory of surviving the event.

Tommy gives Embry a three-part response to small mistakes: stop, make safe, then repair what can be repaired.
Candidate scene: the sequence is attached to the screw spill and practiced with a harmless misplaced part. It is an action rule, not a promise that no harm will occur.
people: Embry Lawson, Tommy Lawson; concepts: repair
Setting: age band 04-10. Situation: Tommy gives Embry a three-part response to small mistakes: stop, make safe, then repair what can be repaired. Trigger: Tommy names a repeatable cleanup sequence. Stakes: The rule becomes both resilience tool and later fuel for excessive checking.
Emotions: guilt, trust. Intensity: 4/5. Regulation: compartmentalization and concealment control. Conflict: 
Theory of mind: belief: Embry believes a mistake can have a procedure after it happens. Trigger: Tommy names a repeatable cleanup sequence. Consequence: The rule becomes both resilience tool and later fuel for excessive checking.

Tommy demonstrates launcher angle, eye protection, distance, and a clear zone during a child-appropriate rocket activity.
Candidate scene: he names where bodies may stand, who calls the launch, and when the setup is considered safe. Embry repeats the boundary back.
people: Embry Lawson, Tommy Lawson; concepts: boundary, safety boundary
Setting: age band 04-10. Situation: Tommy demonstrates launcher angle, eye protection, distance, and a clear zone during a child-appropriate rocket activity. Trigger: Tommy prepares a supervised rocket activity. Stakes: Safety procedure becomes part of shared enjoyment rather than exclusion.
Emotions: trust. Intensity: 2/5. Regulation: controlled action and selective disclosure. Conflict: Embry knows launches require angle control, distance, and a clear zone.
Theory of mind: boundary: Embry knows launches require angle control, distance, and a clear zone. Trigger: Tommy prepares a supervised rocket activity. Consequence: Safety procedure becomes part of shared enjoyment rather than exclusion.
